spec.name: design-stability
spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @f2cd7e3a: the design was corrected there; plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability` and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize `design stability`: the design is the fixed target while a plan realizes it; a change never moves a shard a running plan builds against, it is appended and realized by a following plan sequenced after the work it depends on, so every plan finishes against the goal it began with; only a running plan found built on a shard that is itself wrong stops, the design is corrected once, and the planner rectifies or rebuilds the plan before work resumes. At census the skills say otherwise: design/skill.ts's `yield ≠ ∅ ⇒ amend(C) ⟨intake at INCEPTION ∧ live …⟩` amends at once whatever plan stands on the concept; deliver's `finding ⇒ fold ≺ self's next dispatch ∨ judge ∨ close` does the same mid-plan (deliver-loop removes that line; this unit states the law where it lives, in design and plan); plan/skill.ts's drift laws treat every amendment under a bound plan as a response owed now, and nothing says how a plan stops or resumes.
THE LOOP (the contract the workflow units of this plan each state their own share of; the shards say what must hold, this is how). (1) The architect cuts a shard and dispatches the planner with it; the planner plans it and, when no plan is bound, binds it, returning only the plan's name. (2) The architect dispatches one integrator for the bound plan, named for the plan and kept warm across its waves where the harness can message a finished delegate (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch; omp: agent messaging); the integrator records each ready unit active as it hands out its address and returns only addresses, `<unit> of <plan>`. (3) The architect dispatches one implementer per address, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address and nothing it wrote itself. The implementer reads its spec, builds on its own branch, runs only its unit's own checks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that address to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; what it doubts or meets beside the path it captures as a note. (4) The architect dispatches the assayer with the address and commit. The assayer reads the shard the unit realizes and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect hands the address and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it records the unit completed, commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec, and returns the unit as whole with the newly ready addresses. Red or a merge conflict: it leaves the line as it was and returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. It never repairs, never reads to judge, and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed and the whole holds, the integrator closes the plan and asks the operator to release the line to main: a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command. It never moves main. (8) The architect never runs `plan show <unit>`, and never reads a spec, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. Unit names reach it only as addresses, from the integrator and on verdicts. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing; it is amended into the design only after that plan closes, and a following plan realizes it. A change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the architect finds the bound plan built on a shard that is itself wrong does it stop the plan: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies the plan (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds it; the architect then retracts the note and work resumes.
The pinned version stays the only head while its plan runs under (9), so the assayer reading the current shard reads the pinned one; the runtime, `pin` and `view` need no change. Drift of a bound plan's unit then arises only from a wrong-shard correction, which is exactly when the planner owes the response the drift laws describe.
CHANGE. (1) packages/canon/src/skills/design/skill.ts: state (9) in the design's own vocabulary. The `yield ≠ ∅ ⇒ amend(C)` law becomes: a finding bearing on a concept a bound plan realizes is captured (note) and amended at that plan's close, and a following plan realizes it; any other finding is amended at once (intake stays at inception and live). A wrong shard under a bound plan: capture a note blocking the plan, amend once, the planner rectifies or rebuilds, retract the note. `self` reads every input as a hypothesis rectified against expertise and industry practice (the operator's included). The description says so in one clause.
(2) packages/canon/src/skills/plan/skill.ts (the planner's skill; plan's closure reaches the integrator through deliver): the planner binds its plan at ratification when no plan is bound (the procedure line `plan ≜ … → ratify @ planner` gains `→ bind`), never while one is; `advance` is recorded by the integrator (active at hand-out, completed on green) and `close` by the integrator when every unit is completed; `show(unit)` (a spec) is the planner's and the implementer's read and never the architect's, who meets units only as addresses; `drifted ∨ suspect ⇒ SURFACE` gains that under a bound plan this arises from a stop, and the planner's response (repin, revise, retract, add, or rebuild) precedes the note's retraction; `reconcile ⊨ self` keeps the architect's decision and says the planner prepares a unit's reconciled fields and the integrator records (the concept `skill routing` gives reconciliation to the architect; see the plan's hypothesis to Main). HARD BUDGET: plan weighs 9922 characters on the hook-cap gate at census, 78 under Claude's 10,000 cap; its weighed size must not grow, so pay every added character with a cut in the same cell.
(3) packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/planner.ts: reserves gain bind-at-ratification and rectify-or-rebuild on a stop; writes stays spec (plus the plan records of its own authoring).
(4) If a renamed or added symbol makes packages/canon/test/symbol-altitude.test.ts report a divergence, classify it in its LEDGER with the reason. (5) .changeset/design-stability.md (@cratylus/canon minor). No new test file.
